title: Layout Data Model File
description: ADR 0008 rev 4 on ADR 0009. One file holds one layout: what a person states, nested by scope, every relation a name. Transports, code lines, I/O encodings, processors and CMRInet Nodes are entities; a binding is a route on a bus owner. Stations are derived and absent. Absent is absent. Nothing here names a sheet, a net, a reference or a KiCad symbol unit. Version 3.1.0 (2026-10-25) adds each interlocking's appliances and track (the trackplan piece) and geometry, and the layout's glyphs (ADR 0010); a 3.0.0 file migrates to 3.1.0 by its schema string alone (v3.1.0-migration.md).

name.description: An entity's own name within its scope: case preserved, compared case-folded, never a colon or a slash, no leading or trailing space, no line break or tab.

qualifiedName.description: A reference to an entity of an interlocking scope: the interlocking's name, a colon, the entity's name. Always this form, in every scope (ADR 0008 §4.5).

layoutName.description: A reference to an entity of the layout scope (an interlocking, office unit, transport, code line, I/O encoding or processor): its bare name.

route.description: A device pin's binding: bus owner, address on that bus, driver pin. Three segments: a processor's bus, processor/address/pin (Sargent/0x20/B1). Four: a CMRInet Node's bus, transport/UA/IB.n or OB.n/pin (CMRInet/30/OB.7/D). The segment count tells the owner's kind (ADR 0009 §3.3, §3.5).

namedMap.description: A dictionary keyed by entity name.

settings.description: Every other field a person states on the entity, keyed as drawn (Topic, Broker, hold_ms, Color); values are strings. Which ones apply is reference data (ADR 0008 §4.7).

layout.description: The layout and its layout-scope entities. name, railroad, region, era and rulebook are the Railroad symbol's facts (owner's ruling 2026-10-23).

region.description: The prototype region the layout models; not division or subdivision, which are terms of art.

transport.description: A mechanism (ADR 0009 §3.4): a broker, a serial port and baud, DC pulses. Declared once; placed once per processor that connects to it, and those processors are its anchors.

kind.description: A transport kind key in the reference data: MQTT, CMRI, TIMECODE, LOCONET.

anchors.description: The processors on which an instance of this transport is drawn: the ones that run the code for an encoding riding it. A FieldUnit reaches its code line's transport through the code line; that is derived, not written.

nodes.description: CMRInet Nodes on this line, keyed by UA; a CMRInet Node's identity is transport plus UA (ADR 0009 §3.5). Only on a transport of kind CMRI.

cmrinetNode.description: A CMRInet Node: a driver on the line that provides a bus for its bits (ADR 0009 §3.5). The compiler checks the declared bytes cover the bits used (bits numbered from 1); it never invents them.

bits.description: The bits in use, keyed IB.n or OB.n (direction from the bit's pin type); each is a driver with one pin D.

encodingInstance.description: An encoding riding a transport instance (ADR 0009 §3.4): a code line (codelines{}) or remote I/O (ioEncodings{}). processor is the anchor of the transport instance it rides.

encoding.description: An encoding kind key in the reference data: AAR, USS506, BITS, JMRI, CMRI.

settings.description: topic, chart, version, ... with macros expanded.

processor.description: What runs a FieldUnit's or OfficeUnit's logic and anchors its connections (ADR 0009 §3.3). Its drivers are keyed by their address on its bus.

board.description: A board key in the reference data; it also says whether the generator makes firmware or an application.

ic.description: A driver key in the reference data: MCP23017, PCA9685, MAX7313, GPIO, MQTT-JMRI, ...

kind.description: An encoded driver's object class, stated by its symbol: a JMRI TURNOUT, SENSOR, SIGNALMAST or LIGHT. Such a driver carries no address of its own; its key is kind.name of the device it serves (ADR 0005 S4, R11) unless an Address is drawn to override it.

codeline.description: The one code line this FieldUnit attaches to (ADR 0009 §3.8).

appliances.description: The trackplan's named things by name (ADR 0010 §4.1).

fieldUnit.description: The FieldUnit of an interlocking: the processor that runs its logic (ADR 0009 §3.3). Absent when the drawing does not say.

house.description: An instrument house at a control point; on a US&S 506 line it is a field station, addressed by its column (derived, not written).

device.description: One row of devices[]: one device instance, without identity (ADR 0008 §4.5).

style.description: Always a sorted list, one shape for one fact (ADR 0008 §4.8).

serves.description: The appliance this device serves; for a head device, its mast.

head.description: The head letter a head device renders.

shows.description: The indications a lamp shows, OR'd.

column.description: The office unit column a panel device sits in; a model board device has none.

address.description: The device's own address on a chain (a pixel index).

function.description: The device pin, polarity marks removed.

invert.description: The instance polarity override: the device's Invert field names this pin (FieldUnit ADR 0005 layer 3, Subdivision ADR 0003 D6). Absent when not inverted.

officeUnit.description: An OfficeUnit (never machine): its style, the processor that runs it, its columns and its panel devices. Its field stations are derived from its interlockings and columns.

column.description: A logical column tied to a control point (owner's ruling 2026-10-23). house when CP Name is stated; interlocking alone when it is not (read from the folder).

provenance.description: A property of the file about the whole layout and nothing below it: what produced this file and the one source it was compiled from, the KiCad project.

path.description: The project file, relative to its repository.

polyline.description: Ordered vertices, SVG points syntax: 'x,y x,y ...'. A string because a JSON list is sorted by the canonical form.

glyphKey.description: The drawing's own name for a glyph: library and symbol, 'Railroad-Trackplan:Switch_Lock'. The library's version is in provenance.

placement.description: Where a glyph sits: its anchor (the glyph's origin, which is its bottom-left pin) on the page, its turn (degrees, counter-clockwise as seen on the page, 0/90/180/270) and its mirror (x: top for bottom; y: left for right), applied mirror first, then turn, then translate; and which glyph.

heads.description: A mast's heads by letter: a head cannot exist alone (view §4).

track.description: One drawn run of track between two things: the circuit it belongs to (absent for dark track) and, where an end is an appliance's track port, that port by name (Luchessa:783.R). An end at a joint or a marker is absent: the circuit's bounds are track's business.

marker.description: A track symbol's placement (a joint, END CTC, NextCP, an industry, a policy sign): its kind as the libraries spell it, its placement and glyph, and the circuit at each of its track pins. It joins its track row by name where the symbol has one, else by kind, circuits and ports.

circuits.description: The circuit at each track pin of the marker, by pin name; a pin on dark track is absent.

name.description: The track row's name, where the symbol has one: the marker joins its row by it.

ports.description: The track row's ports, where the symbol has no name: the marker joins its row by kind, circuits and ports.

stroke.description: KiCad's stroke, written only where it is not the default: a width in millimetres (KiCad's 0 means 'the default, which depends on context' and is not written), a dash type other than solid.

fill.description: KiCad's fill, written only where there is one: outline (the stroke colour), background (the sheet's body colour) or a colour of its own.

primitive.description: One drawn element of a glyph, in the glyph's frame: millimetres, x right, y down, the anchor pin at 0,0.

oneOf.description: A circular arc through three points, as KiCad states it.
An axis-aligned rectangle by two opposite corners.
Fixed text that is part of the picture (the H of a hand-thrown switch). A field shown through the symbol is not a primitive: the Layout Data Model File carries the field.

glyph.description: One picture, stated once: its ports (every pin, by name, in the glyph's frame; the anchor pin is 0,0) and its shape. The shape is a list and the canonical form sorts it: drawing order is not a fact.

glyphs.description: layout.glyphs: every glyph any interlocking's geometry names, by glyph key; nothing the layout does not draw.

mileposts.description: Milepost anchors by milepost (ADR 0004 D7: the Value is the milepost, so it is the marker's name). Luchessa draws two; Sargent none.

portRef.description: A switch's track port, or a pin of a named track symbol, by qualified name: the switch or symbol, a dot, and the pin (a switch's C, N or R, a derail's C or R; an industry's EoT): Luchessa:783.R, Luchessa:Gilroy Industry.EoT.

appliance.description: A named thing on the trackplan (ADR 0010 §4.1, by Role APPLIANCE): a switch or derail, a mast with its heads, a track circuit, a lamp or a contact. Keyed by its Name; geometry's appliances{} uses the same keys. A reference to another interlocking's appliance (a qualified name drawn here) is not an appliance of this one. Derived things stay out: a switch's gang and a derail's dependence follow from the names (ADR 0003 D8); signals, routes and limits are the evaluator's.

style.description: The symbol's Style: a switch's powered, lock, dual, manual, manual_sensed or derail; a mast's single, double or dwarf; a lamp's maintainer_call or non_vital; a circuit's virtual.

milepost.description: The milepost the symbol states, optional geographic context (a hot box alarm's location, for the timetable).

controlPoint.description: The house (control point) the appliance belongs to: its own CP field where it states one; else the one house of its interlocking; else, with two or more houses, the house its chain of relations reaches (a gang's switch without a letter to its other switches and derails, a switch to its OS circuit, a mast and its signal joint, a signal joint to the circuits beside it that hold no switch, a circuit across a plain joint, a virtual circuit's members to it, a maintainer call by its MC wire).

osCircuit.description: The circuit a switch's or derail's track carries: its OS circuit (the circuit's marker, or else the switch's TC, whose library default is the switch's name and T1, ADR 0003 D3). Absent on dark track.

indicationCeiling.description: The best indication over the switch, as drawn (STOP/RESTRICTING).

heads.description: A mast's heads by letter, each with the Style the trackplan draws (ADR 0009 §3.7).

members.description: A virtual track circuit's member circuits, as its IndicationToken lists them.

trackSymbol.description: A track symbol (a joint, an end, a policy sign) as a row: its Kind as the libraries spell it, and the circuits and named pins at its pins. An end may have a name (an industry); a signal joint adds the mast standing on it and its control point; a NextCP the interlocking it leads to; a policy sign its Direction.

name.description: The symbol's name where it has one (an industry); geometry's marker carries the same.

circuits.description: The circuit at each track pin, by pin name (A, B; CTC, DARK; To; Track; EoT); a pin on dark track is absent. The same map geometry's markers[] carries, so a marker joins its row here by kind and circuits (ADR 0010 C6).

ports.description: Where a pin's track meets, with nothing between, a switch port or a pin of a named track symbol: by pin name. This is the only record of track that has no circuit (dark track).

controlPoint.description: A signal joint's control point: its CP field, or its mast's, or the interlocking's one house.

interlocking.description: A NextCP's destination: the interlocking its track leads to, which may lie beyond the layout (Lick, Hollister).

trackplan.description: The interlocking's track as the netlist states it, by circuit and port name, never by coordinate (ADR 0010 C6). A circuit is the track between joints and ends, joined through a switch's or derail's ports; dark track has no circuit.

joints.description: IRJ and IRJ_SIGNAL: insulated joints, each between the circuits on its A and B pins; a signal joint's A pin is where the route it protects begins, inside the interlocking.

ends.description: END_CTC, NEXT_CP, BUMPER, INDUSTRY: where the drawn track ends, and what lies beyond.

policies.description: The policy signs (RULE_105, RULE_251, RULE_261, RULE_93) with their Direction, on the circuit at their pin.

links.description: Switch ports that meet with no joint or end between them (Luchessa:795.R and Luchessa:795D.R), with the circuit there.

mileposts.description: The milepost anchors drawn on the trackplan, by name (their milepost); geometry places them.
